summary: American missionary Renee Bach founded the charity Serving His Children in Jinja, Uganda, and with no medical training treated malnourished children herself, including blood transfusions; mothers sued her over more than 100 child deaths.

evidence.note: arrives in Uganda at 18 in September 2007; birth year inferred from this
founds Serving His Children as a feeding program in Masese, Jinja
medium post says she treated sick children herself with no medical training
civil suit on behalf of mothers over deaths of more than 100 children, pending at release
2011 blog post on a transfusion causing an anaphylactic reaction in an infant
she bags an infant with oxygen while driving; the baby later died
local missionary community and her Jinja church defended her against critics
charity paused in 2015 after criminal complaints, then reopened
social worker reports a 2018 infant death after Bach's intervention
extended discussion of white saviorism and attitudes toward Uganda

notes: Birth year approximate: she was 18 on arrival in September 2007, so 1988 or 1989. No role fits an untrained person practising real medicine; quack-fake-healer is closest. medical-malpractice chosen over quackery because the treatments were real medicine done by an unqualified person. Kony 2012 intro treated as comparison, not covered time.
